title: Eventual cohomology stabilization gives stalk injectivity for a derived limit
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, let $(K_n)$ be an inverse system in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, and let $(K,p,\delta)$ be a derived limit of it [def-weil-derived-limit], written $K=R\varprojlim_nK_n$ (any one; derived limits are not unique up to canonical isomorphism). Let $x\in X$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$. Suppose there are an index $n(x)$ and a fundamental system $\mathfrak U_x$ of open neighborhoods of $x$ such that, for every $U\in\mathfrak U_x$, (i) $R^1\varprojlim_n H^{m-1}(U,K_n)=0$, and (ii) for every $n\ge n(x)$ the transition map $H^m(U,K_n)\to H^m(U,K_{n(x)})$ is injective. Then the map on stalks $H^m(K)_x\to H^m(K_{n(x)})_x$ induced by $\mathrm{pr}_{n(x)}\circ p:K\to K_{n(x)}$ is injective. Here cohomology is sheaf cohomology on opens [pqf-def-cohomology].

proof.text: Let $\gamma\in H^m(K)_x$ map to zero in $H^m(K_{n(x)})_x$ under the map induced by $\mathrm{pr}_{n(x)}\circ p$. By [lem-pc-ringed-space-sheafification-cohomology], choose an open neighborhood $U_0$ of $x$ and a class $\widetilde\gamma_0\in H^m(U_0,K)$ representing $\gamma$. Its image in $H^m(K_{n(x)})_x$ is zero, so the final clause of that node (applied to $K_{n(x)}$) lets us shrink to an open $U_1\subseteq U_0$ containing $x$ on which the image of $\widetilde\gamma_0$ in $H^m(U_1,K_{n(x)})$ is zero. Since $\mathfrak U_x$ is a fundamental system, choose $U\in\mathfrak U_x$ with $U\subseteq U_1$, and let $\widetilde\gamma\in H^m(U,K)$ be the restriction of $\widetilde\gamma_0$; it still represents $\gamma$, and its image $\widetilde\gamma_{n(x)}\in H^m(U,K_{n(x)})$ is zero, being a restriction of zero. Hypotheses (i) and (ii) therefore apply to this $U$.

For this $U\in\mathfrak U_x$, the short exact sequence of [lem-pc-ringed-space-rgamma-derived-limit] gives $0\to R^1\varprojlim_n H^{m-1}(U,K_n)\to H^m(U,K)\to\varprojlim_n H^m(U,K_n)\to0$, whose right map has components $H^m(U,\mathrm{pr}_n\circ p)$. The left term is zero by hypothesis (i). The map from the inverse limit on the right to $H^m(U,K_{n(x)})$ is injective: a compatible family whose $n(x)$-component is zero has zero $n$-component for every $n\ge n(x)$ by hypothesis (ii), and each earlier component is the image of the zero $n(x)$-component under the transition maps. Since $\widetilde\gamma_{n(x)}=0$, $\widetilde\gamma$ maps to zero in the inverse limit and therefore is zero.

proof.text: Since the representative restricts to zero on a neighborhood of $x$, its germ $\gamma$ is zero. Thus the natural map $H^m(R\varprojlim_nK_n)_x\to H^m(K_{n(x)})_x$ is injective.
